metric: S(dx,dy)=1-sum(|O-Nshift|)/(W*H*4*255); 4-channel denominator, per-pixel abs diff, integer shifts
shift_reading: (dx,dy) = how far new's content must move to line up with old
search: brute force integer (dx,dy) in [-R,R]^2, step 1, full canvas, no downsampling
boundary_rule: argmin on |dx|=R or |dy|=R -> rerun with R'=2R; boundary=true if still on edge
gate_reused: 0.99 (Go gatePassed); this script does NOT modify gatePassed or similarityNormalized
positive_controls: C1 real-data edge-shift of new.png; C2 synthetic noise; C0 S(0,0) must equal go report.json
scope: diagnosis only: reported (dx,dy) are measurement results, NOT renderer constants
field_semantics_boundary_vs_probe_bounda: report.json carries TWO DIFFERENT boundary fields. boundary = the ZERO-PADDED (band) metric argmax sits on the search edge. THIS is the field that governs the reported ceiling; it is False on all 16 rows. probe_boundary = the BAND-FREE (integral-image) metric argmax sits on the search edge; True on 8 of 16 rows. probe_boundary=True does NOT mean those 8 rows were judged invalid and does NOT invalidate the table: the reported ceiling is max(band, noband), and for a NEGATIVE verdict (reaches_gate=false) taking the max is the SAFE direction - a higher ceiling that still misses 0.99 is stronger evidence, not weaker. Sources: .audit/align_ceiling.py lines 327-328. Report.json field names were deliberately NOT renamed: it is evidence.
